title: Practice Pack: Motion
subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
instructions: Level 1 checks the ideas, Level 2 is board-style numericals, and Level 3 is Foundation-level challenge.
In every numerical: write the given values, convert units (km/h → m/s: divide by 3.6), write the formula, substitute, and give the answer with its unit.
Equations of motion: v = u + at · s = ut + ½at^{2} · v^{2} – u^{2} = 2as

questions.q: Define displacement. Can the displacement of a body be zero when the distance it has covered is not zero? Give an example.
questions.answer: Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position, in a stated direction. Yes: if a body returns to its starting point, for example one full round of a circular track, its displacement is zero but the distance covered is not.

questions.q: A body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. What kind of motion is this?
What does the slope of a distance–time graph tell us?
questions.answer: The speed of the body. A steeper slope means a higher speed.

questions.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph give?
questions.answer: The displacement (equal to the distance for motion in one direction along a straight line).

questions.q: Is uniform circular motion accelerated? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. The speed is constant, but the direction of motion changes at every point, so the velocity changes and the motion is accelerated.

questions.q: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. Find its average speed in km/h and in m/s.
questions.answer: Average speed = 150 km/3 h = 50 km/h = 50/3.6 ≈ 13.9 m/s.

questions.q: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of diameter 200 m in 40 s. What distance has he covered, and what is his displacement, at the end of 2 minutes 20 seconds? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.answer: Time = 140 s = 3.5 rounds. Circumference = (22/7) × 200 ≈ 628.6 m, so distance = 3.5 × 628.6 = 2200 m. After 3.5 rounds he is at the opposite end of a diameter, so displacement = 200 m.

questions.q: A bus slows down from 80 km/h to 60 km/h in 5 s. Find its acceleration.
questions.answer: u = 80/3.6 ≈ 22.2 m/s, v = 60/3.6 ≈ 16.7 m/s. a = (v – u)/t = (16.7 – 22.2)/5 ≈ –1.1 m/s^{2}. The negative sign shows retardation.

questions.q: A train starting from rest reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 5 minutes. Find its acceleration and the distance it travels in this time.
A car accelerates uniformly from 18 km/h to 36 km/h in 5 s. Find (i) the acceleration and (ii) the distance covered in that time.
A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest with a uniform retardation of 4 m/s^{2}. Find the time taken and the stopping distance.
A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 42,250 km and takes 24 hours to go around the Earth once. Find its speed.
A car covers the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. Find its average speed for the whole journey. (Hint: it is NOT 50 km/h.)
questions.answer: Let each half be d km. Time = d/40 + d/60 = 5d/120 = d/24 h. Average speed = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h. (For equal distances, average speed = 2v_{1}v_{2}/(v_{1} + v_{2}).)

questions.q: Car A starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s^{2} for 5 s. Car B starts from rest and accelerates at 1 m/s^{2} for 10 s. Which car ends with the greater speed, and which covers the greater distance?
questions.answer: A: v = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s, s = ½ × 2 × 25 = 25 m. B: v = 1 × 10 = 10 m/s, s = ½ × 1 × 100 = 50 m. Both end at the same speed (10 m/s), but B covers twice the distance.

questions.q: A velocity–time graph is a straight line rising from 0 to 20 m/s in the first 4 s, then horizontal at 20 m/s for the next 6 s. Find the acceleration in the first 4 s and the total distance covered in 10 s.
questions.answer: a = 20/4 = 5 m/s^{2}. Distance = area under the graph = triangle (½ × 4 × 20 = 40 m) + rectangle (6 × 20 = 120 m) = 160 m.

closing: Check every answer for units. That's where most marks go missing!
